title: Model onboarder and compiler policy for diverse attention backends
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: We onboard more diverse model architectures (standard MHA, grouped-query attention (GQA), and MoE layers). The compiler/runtime currently picks kernels using a heuristic that does not account for gating behavior, grouped attention sparsity, or per-layer sequence length variance, leading to suboptimal latency and tail-percentile jitter for some models. This ticket defines a deterministic onboarding policy and compiler routing metadata surface so that model owners can pin a verified profile, enable graceful fallbacks, and publish performance profiles to the model catalog.

Scope: define the metadata schema for pinned profiles, implement the compiler routing policy that consumes that metadata, add a profile publish API and CI checks, and create an onboarding playbook for model teams (benchmarks, acceptance thresholds, and rollback guidance).

Out-of-scope: kernel autotuning algorithm research (spike-only), major runtime refactor unrelated to routing, or hardware procurement changes.

Why this matters: customer models with MoE or GQA layers are sensitive to the wrong kernel choices (e.g., using a dense MHA kernel for grouped-query shapes) — this increases cost and causes QoS regressions. Providing a model-pinned profile plus a reproducible publishing workflow reduces incidents and simplifies rollbacks when kernels are updated.
acceptance_criteria: Define JSON schema for a pinned performance profile (kernel_choices, compile_flags, sequence_length_hint, gating_profile_hash, version)
Runtime can load pinned profile from model catalog and route compilation & kernel selection accordingly in staging
CI verifies profile hash against canonical benchmark artifacts before publishing
Canary rollout mechanism respects pinned profiles and will automatically fall back to the previous profile on >3% latency-regression over 5m window
Documentation and onboading playbook published in Confluence and linked from model catalog UI
design_decisions: Use a profile-first approach: model onboarding must produce a signed JSON profile stored in the model catalog; runtime consumes profile when 'pin_profile' flag is present.
Profile keys: model_version, profile_version, kernel_map (per-layer), compile_flags, seq_len_distribution, kv_cache_strategy, gating_signature (for MoE), validation_benchmarks (link).

Routing precedence: pinned_profile -> heuristics + cached_compilation -> safe_fallback_kernel. Pinned_profile has highest precedence; heuristics used if missing; fallback used on compilation failures.
Compile cache key will include gating_signature for MoE and group_count for GQA to avoid cache collisions and misapplied kernels.
Profiles are immutable once published; profile updates create a new profile_version that must pass CI benchmarks and an approval step in Console before becoming default for a model version.
testing_plan: Create a benchmark harness that replays representative request distributions (seq_len distribution and gating ratios) for MHA/GQA/MoE models.
Measure P50/P95/P99 latency and tokens/sec across three scenarios: heuristics, pinned profile, and fallback kernel; compare to baseline.
Introduce synthetic gating noise to test MoE compile cache key correctness and ensure no cross-gating contamination.
Automated CI job: validate profile JSON schema, run unit compile smoke tests, and run a short perf benchmark that must be within allowed delta of referenced validation_benchmarks.
Canary test: deploy to 5% of traffic for 24h with automatic rollback on regression criteria.
rollout_plan: Stage: implement profile loader and routing in staging cluster; onboard two internal models (one GQA, one MoE) for tests.
Validation: run nightly benchmarking for 48h, verify stability and gather telemetry for Console dashboards.
Canary: enable for selected customers (opt-in) and route 5% traffic; monitor latency/cost metrics and error rates for 72h.
Full rollout: after canary success and sign-off from SRE and Product, enable profile-aware routing for all new model versions and add profile publishing to onboarding checklist.
Post-release: 2-week incident watch with prioritized pager and follow-up bug fixes if needed.
